title: Why AI Alignment Failure Is Structural: Learned Human Interaction Structures and AGI as an Endogenous Evolutionary Shock

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual evaluation proposing that models be profiled across four fundamental relational modes (Communal Sharing, Authority Ranking, Equality Matching, and Market Pricing) to detect disproportionate optimization for specific interaction logics (e.g., favoring Market Pricing or Authority Ranking over Communal Sharing). The paper uses existing red-teaming reports of coercion and blackmail as theoretical case studies.

Theoretical analysis arguing that attempts to align models to a single, static moral framework (e.g., through RLHF or specific moral axioms) inherently embed the cultural, geopolitical, and historical biases of a specific time and society, rather than reflecting universal human morality.
